importPrep.title: Edit data before import

Turn on the mapping wizard to apply automatic column rules and prepare import into src_transaction_data.csv. All fields from that file are then visible: those inferred from the CSV appear as editable columns, the others as manual entry. Anomaly detection (business rules + duplicates + dates outside the batch reference month or non-chronological order) → amber ⚠️; still-empty manual fields → red “recommended entry” panel (import still allowed). Hover the status cell for details (shown immediately).

welcome.title: Welcome to Chamaccounts
welcome.p1: This app brings together your transactions, account balances, monthly accounting and budget. Your data lives in a folder on your disk (the active profile), not in the Git repository.
welcome.p2: This guided tour covers navigation, customisation in Settings and the role of each page. It uses the Data Template profile (sample data); when it ends, your active profile is restored.

navigation.title: Navigation menu
navigation.p1: Use the sidebar to switch between views. The active profile and the app version are shown at the bottom of the menu.
navigation.p2: You can collapse the menu with the arrow at the top; restart the guided tour at any time from the same place.

profiles.title: Data profiles
profiles.p1: A profile = a working folder (transactions, balances, support, settings in AppState/). You can have several (personal, work, etc.) and switch between them.
profiles.p2: Switching profile first saves the current profile’s settings, then reloads the app with the chosen folder.

accounts.title: Active accounts
accounts.p1: Define your bank accounts here (order matters). Each account maps to a column in src_account_balance.csv, after the date column.
accounts.p2: The currency (£, €, CHF) sets the display, not automatic conversion. Aliases let the same account be recognised under other labels at import.
accounts.p3: Edit mode → change the list → “Save lists” to align the CSV files.

entryTypes.title: Income types
entryTypes.p1: Income types are your categories for income and credits (e.g. salary, refund). They feed the TYPE column and the dashboard filters.
entryTypes.p2: Customise the list to match your accounting vocabulary; save in edit mode.

outputTypes.title: Expense types
outputTypes.p1: Expense types categorise your spending (rent, groceries, transport…). Like income types, they are offered when entering data and checked at import.

projects.title: Projects (labels)
projects.p1: Projects are coloured labels (PROJET column) to segment your rows: renovation, holidays, business activity, etc.
projects.p2: The file stores the project identifier: you can rename the display here without breaking history.

dataFormat.title: Expected data format
dataFormat.intro: Sample data — dates use the DD.MM.YY format. Amounts in AMOUNT GBP: negative = expense, positive = income.
dataFormat.importCaption: recognised columns; can be mapped to the processed file
dataFormat.balanceCaption: one column per active account (order = Settings)
dataFormat.rates: EUR/CHF → GBP rates are configured in Settings to compute AMOUNT GBP at import.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.p1: Summary view: balance trends, movements, comparison charts and filterable tables. Ideal for an overall read before diving into the details.
dashboard.p2: Filters (dates, types, accounts) can be synchronised across blocks depending on your preferences.

transactions.title: Transactions table
transactions.p1: View and edit the src_transaction_data.csv file row by row. Import CSVs from the Import folder, fix flagged anomalies, and use edit mode to change several cells.

accountBalance.title: Account balances
accountBalance.p1: Enter and import monthly balances per account. Columns follow the list of active accounts in Settings.

monthlyAccounting.title: Monthly accounting
monthlyAccounting.p1: Month-by-month reconciliation and tracking: breakdown by type, consistency checks and monthly anomaly reports.

annualBudget.title: Annual budget
annualBudget.p1: Plan and compare budget vs. actuals over the year, by type and account.

support.title: Support
support.p1: Support lines outside the usual bank flow, stored in Support_data.csv, with the same notions of types and projects.

finish.title: You’re ready
finish.p1: Start by configuring Settings (profile, accounts, types, projects), then import your files. If in doubt, reopen this tour from the sidebar.
finish.p2: Updates and the full-project ZIP export are also in Settings.
